Research continuation completed across 2B–8B; 1B remains unchanged. No scores assigned.

The environment prevented local inspection or writes (`bwrap: ... NEWADDR`), so the manifest update could not be persisted. Apply these additions/disposition changes to `research-ledger-manifest.json`.

### New evidence units

- `EX-44` — **2B**: Mexico–US March 9, 2023 joint statement launched phase two of the Bicentennial Framework, targeting fentanyl, weapons trafficking, and transnational crime. Direct presidential-hosted security cooperation. [Presidencia](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/prensa/joint-statement-mexico-united-states)
- `EX-45` — **2B**: October 2023 High-Level Security Dialogue recorded continued bilateral cooperation and future goals under the Bicentennial Framework. Contrary to a complete Mérida-cooperation breakdown. [Mexican SRE](https://www.gob.mx/sre/en/articulos/foreign-secretary-alicia-barcena-takes-part-in-the-mexico-us-high-level-security-dialogue-at-the-national-palace)
- `EX-46` — **2B**: Mexico’s September 2023 UN statement supported international law, diplomacy, and peaceful resolution in Ukraine. [Mexican UN mission](https://mision.sre.gob.mx/onu/images/2023/CSONU/Intervenciones/20Sep23_-_Statement_delivered_by_the_Secretary_of_Foreign_Affairs_SCUN_Ukraine.pdf)

- `EX-47` — **3B**: INEGI preliminary registered-death statistics provide the authoritative January–December 2023 homicide dataset. [INEGI](https://en.www.inegi.org.mx/app/saladeprensa/noticia/9207)
- `EX-48` — **3B**: Mexico’s security ministry reported a 20% reduction in intentional homicide over the administration’s period through December 2023. Government claim; retain with attribution caveat. [SSPC](https://www.gob.mx/sspc/prensa/disminuye-20-homicidio-doloso-355856)
- `EX-49` — **3B/6B/8B**: UN OCHA’s Otis Situation Report recorded the 25 October 2023 Category 5 disaster, deaths, missing persons, destroyed homes, and armed-forces-led response. [UN OCHA](https://www.unocha.org/publications/report/mexico/mexico-hurricane-otis-situation-report-no-01-8-november-2023)
- `EX-50` — **3B/6B**: CONEVAL’s August 2023 health-rights study documented access problems among people without social security during the government’s health-system reforms. [CONEVAL](https://www.coneval.org.mx/InformesPublicaciones/Paginas/Mosaicos/Analisis_cualitativo_salud_2023.aspx)

- `EX-51` — **4B**: SCJN officially invalidated Plan B’s second electoral-reform package by nine votes, citing serious legislative-procedure violations. [SCJN](https://www.internet2.scjn.gob.mx/red2/comunicados/noticia.asp?id=7408)
- `EX-52` — **4B**: INE and federal authorities publicly maintained institutional coordination for the 2023–24 electoral process, contrary evidence of continuing institutional resilience. [INE](https://www.reddit.com/r/mexico_politics/comments/14a3s95/ine-comunicado-ine-y-presidencia-de-la-rep%C3%BAblica-fortalecen-colaboraci%C3%B3n-de-cara-al-proceso-electoral-federal-2024/)
- `EX-53` — **4B**: Mexico’s Women’s Political Participation Observatory adopted a 2023 work program and transferred its presidency from INE to INMUJERES. [INMUJERES/OPPMM](https://www.gob.mx/historico-instituto/prensa/programa-de-trabajo-2023-del-observatorio-de-participacion-politica-de-las-mujeres-en-mexico)

- `EX-54` — **5B**: INEGI reported 3.2% real annual GDP growth in 2023, separating the official outcome from earlier sub-1% commentary. [INEGI result reported by El Economista](https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/amp/economia/El-PIB-de-Mexico-crecio-3.1-en-2023-Inegi-20240130-0031.html)
- `EX-55` — **5B/6B**: CONASAMI’s 2023 minimum-wage resolution raised the general daily wage to 207.44 pesos and the northern-border wage to 312.41 pesos, both by 20%. [EY summary of CONASAMI resolution](https://www.ey.com/es_mx/technical/tax/boletines-fiscales/aumento-al-salario-minimo-2023)
- `EX-56` — **5B/8B**: AP documented Maya Train partial opening on 15 December 2023, hours-long delays, incomplete track, and major cost escalation; AMLO acknowledged missing components and uncertain operating-cost recovery. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/7b0db1b6b262acde6721debceaa5af7e)

- `EX-57` — **6B**: April 2023 government report recorded 11,408,304 elderly pension beneficiaries and 449,822 Sembrando Vida participants across 21 states. [Secretaría de Bienestar](https://www.gob.mx/bienestar/prensa/presenta-ariadna-montiel-avance-de-pensiones-y-programas-para-el-bienestar-contribuyen-a-la-felicidad)
- `EX-58` — **6B**: December 2023 report stated Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro reached 2.8 million cumulative beneficiaries and exceeded its six-year target by 500,000. [STPS](https://www.gob.mx/stps/prensa/supera-en-medio-millon-de-personas-meta-de-atencion-el-programa-jovenes-construyendo-el-futuro?idiom=es-MX)
- `EX-59` — **6B**: October 2023 agreement with 23 states federalized IMSS-Bienestar under a universal, public, free-care objective, directly linking the reform to AMLO’s administration. [IMSS](https://www.gob.mx/imss/prensa/gobierno-de-mexico-y-23-estados-firman-acuerdo-nacional-para-la-federalizacion-del-sistema-de-salud-para-el-bienestar)

- `EX-60` — **7B**: Mexico’s 2023 federal public-account annex lists active trust funds, their balances, income, expenditures, and responsible authorities; use the Sedena/FAMI row rather than relying only on press summaries. [Federal public account, Annex I](https://www.cuentapublica.hacienda.gob.mx/work/models/CP/2023/tomo/III/E_IIFMA.pdf)
- `EX-61` — **7B/8B**: ASF audit material identifies SEDENA as responsible for supervising application of trust-fund resources. This supports authority/accountability, but does not itself prove AMLO personal benefit. [ASF audit](https://www.asf.gob.mx/Trans/Informes/IR2023c/Documentos/Auditorias/2023_0151_a.pdf)
- `EX-62` — **7B**: El Universal records AMLO’s contemporaneous statement that he was “absolutely sure” there was no conflict of interest in the José Ramón López Beltrán matter. Retain as contrary/self-exculpatory evidence, not proof of innocence. [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/amlo-estoy-absolutamente-seguro-que-no-hay-conflicto-de-interes-en-caso-de-mi-hijo/)

- `EX-63` — **8B**: AMLO’s official 15 December 2023 Maya Train inauguration records the project’s partial opening and army-engineer role. Treat inauguration as execution milestone only, not achieved-outcome evidence. [Presidencia](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/prensa/president-amlo-leads-the-inaugural-run-of-the-maya-train-first-stage)
- `EX-64` — **8B**: AP’s same-period reporting documents incomplete construction, delays, cost escalation, and uncertain operating-cost recovery, supplying the required contrary implementation evidence. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/7b0db1b6b262acde6721debceaa5af7e)
- `EX-65` — **8B**: December 2023 STPS report records a measurable program-delivery milestone for Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro. [STPS](https://www.gob.mx/stps/prensa/supera-en-medio-millon-de-personas-meta-de-atencion-el-programa-jovenes-construyendo-el-futuro?idiom=es-MX)

### Required manifest changes

Add the 22 IDs above with their chapter/lens mappings. Also change the following older items:

- Mark duplicate chapter-specific recreations of the same OCHA, CONASAMI, Maya Train, FAMI, and Ayotzinapa claims as `superseded_duplicate`; retain the global `EX-*` item as canonical.
- Change the prior “Mérida discontinued” item from unqualified `final_evidence` to `context` or `qualified_final_evidence`; the new official 2023 evidence shows continued Bicentennial security cooperation.
- Change inauguration-only Maya Train items to `context` or `execution_milestone`; pair them with `EX-56`/`EX-64` for delays, incompleteness, cost, and operating viability.
- Keep family-graft items qualified: allegations and AMLO’s denial do not establish personal enrichment.
- Retain all country-level indicators as `context`, never ruler-attributed evidence by themselves.

### Chapter disposition

- **1B:** unchanged; no discriminating opportunity.
- **2B:** researchable gap materially narrowed. Official evidence supports continued security cooperation and diplomatic restraint; Mérida discontinuation remains only secondarily supported. Shortfall remains for direct mediation outcomes.
- **3B:** improved with official homicide data, government-reported improvement, and Otis evidence. Attribution remains mixed for national outcomes.
- **4B:** improved with SCJN primary ruling, INE institutional-coordination evidence, and women’s political-participation documentation.
- **5B:** improved with official GDP and wage outcomes; project viability remains mixed and requires contrary evidence.
- **6B:** major gap addressed through 2023 program coverage, IMSS-Bienestar federalization, and CONEVAL health-access analysis.
- **7B:** primary financial-record and ASF accountability evidence added; personal-benefit claim remains unresolved.
- **8B:** execution evidence strengthened, but AP’s contemporaneous delays, incompleteness, and cost escalation prevent inauguration from being treated as successful outcome evidence.
